call_points.text: Poultry Healthcare division grew by 41% in Q4 and 21% for the full year, supported by expanded placements.
Gross debt reduced from ₹102 crores to ₹70 crores, leading to a comfortable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x.
Company describes itself as the largest supplier of PPR vaccine and a supplier to the WOAH PPR vaccine bank.
It calls itself the second largest poultry vaccine manufacturer in India with a 35% market share.
Hester Africa runs the GALVmed VITAL 2 project for ruminant vaccine delivery in Kenya, Nigeria and Tanzania.
Management says it is focusing on expanding the Petcare division in India.

operating_notes.text: The company received marketing and manufacturing licences for its H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine during the year.
Mehsana flagship plant capacity is 8.6 Billion Doses annually; Hester Nepal 1.24 Billion and Hester Africa 1.5 Billion.
India network: 15 sales depots, 1,000+ distributors and a 250+ field force.
Company states it is the second largest poultry vaccine manufacturer in India with a 35% market share.
Hester Africa loan from Gates Foundation amended to reduce principal to USD 5 million with interest waiver.
Poultry Healthcare growth was driven by higher institutional business, deeper market penetration and health products launched in FY26
Animal Healthcare was impacted by timing of government-led immunisation programmes, reflecting delays in tender execution
Consolidated profitability was boosted by an exceptional gain of ₹85.3 Cr from the Gates Foundation loan amendment at Hester Africa
Overall capacity utilisation is around 60-65% across the entire manufacturing setup, including the new fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities.
Poultry Healthcare revenue stepped up from ₹45-48 Cr to over ₹60 Cr, driven by market share gains and new products, not price increases.
Consolidated debt was ₹103 Cr as on 30 June 2026, after the Gates Foundation loan was reduced from USD 12 million to USD 5 million and interest waived.

timeline.summary: Mr. Rajiv Gandhi, acting for Hester Biosciences Limited’s promoters, declared no encumbrances on holdings during FY2026 ended 31 March 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹100.11 Cr (+22.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹15.98 Cr (+1138.8% YoY).
Hester Biosciences received requests from promoters Ravin Gandhi and Bela Gandhi to reclassify their stake to public.
Vinod Mali, CFO, shared the earnings conference call recording for Q4FY26 & FY26 results via link on 15 May 2026.
Hester Biosciences released its corporate presentation for FY2025-26, reporting consolidated revenue of ₹332.60 Cr.
Hester Biosciences reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹100.11 Cr and hosted its earnings conference call on 15 May 2026.
Hester Biosciences applied to BSE and NSE on 19 May 2026 for no-objection to reclassify Ravin Gandhi and Bela Gandhi from promoter to public category under Regulation 31A.
20 May 2026: Hester Biosciences announced amendments to Hester Africa's loan agreement with Gates Foundation, reducing outstanding debt to USD 5 million and waiving accrued interest.
Hester Biosciences Ltd’s 39th AGM held on 21 July 2026 via VC, with 56.38% shareholder attendance and all resolutions passed unanimously.
Hester Biosciences Ltd received NSE and BSE no-objection for re-classification of Ravin Gandhi and Bela Gandhi from promoter to public category on 24 July 2026.

Hester Biosciences reported Q1FY27 results with standalone PAT up 88% YoY to ₹147 Cr and consolidated PAT up 459% YoY to ₹96.7 Cr, driven by an exceptional gain of ₹85.3 Cr from Gates Foundation loan waiver.

Hester Biosciences held its Q1FY27 earnings call on 30 July 2026, reporting standalone revenue up 14% and PAT up 88% YoY, consolidated revenue down 8%, and consolidated debt reduced to ₹103 Cr after the Gates Foundation loan amendment.
Hester Biosciences Ltd upgraded credit ratings from BBB to BBB+ (long-term) and A3+ to A2 (short-term) by CARE Ratings on 27 August 2026
Hester Biosciences approved ₹1.05 Cr investment in SLYCE AGRI WORLD LLP for 26% stake to procure captive solar power.
